key_insight: RoboArchitect automates the design of the control software around a frozen robot policy, rather than changing the policy itself. A coding model learns from robot rollouts to diagnose failures and iteratively revise this software.
problem_solved: Robot agent harnesses—which coordinate policy calls, vision tools, and direct arm commands—are typically hand-built and redesigned for each robot or benchmark.
method: Observe robot rollouts to identify where the current agent harness fails.
Use a coding model to diagnose failures and iteratively revise the harness.
Coordinate a frozen robot policy, vision tools, and direct arm control; the supplied abstract does not describe the persistent-memory mechanism named in the title.
impact: Automated harness design offers an alternative to finetuning when adapting robots to new setups. It could reduce manual engineering, though the supplied abstract excerpt provides no quantitative results.
visual_elements: Iteration loop: robot rollout → failure diagnosis → harness revision → new rollout.
Architecture diagram showing a harness routing decisions to a frozen policy, vision tools, or direct arm commands.
Side-by-side workflow: manually redesigned harness versus automated harness development.
Locked policy icon beside editable control code to distinguish harness updates from model finetuning.
paper_title: RoboArchitect: Automating the Design of Robotic Agents with Persistent Memory
paper_authors: Shengguang Wu, Suning Huang, Cherie Ho, Ria Doshi, Hao Zhu
